title: Deterministic Load Signature Runner and Acceptance Playbook for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Deliver a deterministic, tenant-aware load harness (the 'Signature Runner') plus a reproducible benchmarking methodology and a runnable customer acceptance playbook for Dedicated capacity shipments. The goal is to produce objective, repeatable throughput evidence (latency quantiles, CPU/GPU utilization, token cost curves) that can be shared with customers and used as gating criteria for Dedicated SLAs.

Scope:
- Core harness: request generator, replay engine for anonymized customer traces, tenant-mixer, KV-cache priming module, and steady-state sustain controller.
- Measurement: p50/p90/p99/p999 and tail-latency heatmaps, slope-of-throughput vs. offered load, autoscaler-trigger test vectors, and cost-per-token accounting.
- Methodology: seed traces, warmup/priming heuristics, fixture isolation (no co-tenants), statistical repeatability (min 5 runs per profile), and noise-reduction (controlled jitter, clock sync).
- Customer acceptance kit: runnable scripts, conftest/Canary checklist, dashboard links, and a signed SLA evidence bundle customers can use for onboarding signoff.

Non-goals: full e2e tenant mix with noisy neighbors (that is a separate chaotic-testing project), and in-depth model accuracy regressions (handled by Optimize team).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay an anonymized customer trace with <5% variance in median token throughput across 5 repeated runs
Sustained throughput profile documented for chosen Dedicated tier with p99 tail below SLA target (configured per-customer), and reproducible within +/-10%
Autoscaler safety tests that exercise scale-up and scale-down hysteresis complete without missed requests or cache incoherence
Customer acceptance playbook includes: (1) step-by-step run commands; (2) what artifacts to collect; (3) signoff checklist; (4) sample dashboard and signed evidence template
Artifacts (Jupyter notebook, k6/Go harness binaries, and Prometheus+Grafana dashboards) uploaded to the customer onboarding folder and linked from the playbook
test_steps: 1) Select profile: small/medium/large and the target model variant (e.g., rwk-3B-quant)
2) Prime KV cache: run priming script with seeded prompts until cache hit rate stabilizes (>90%)
3) Run warmup for 10 minutes to allow kernel selection and JIT paths to stabilize
4) Execute 5 independent runs of the same trace with controlled inter-run cooldown; collect telemetry (latency histograms, GPU counters, network metrics)
5) Run autoscaler test: step offered RPS up by 30% and hold for 3 minutes, then step down; assert no request loss and acceptable latency increase per hysteresis policy
6) Produce evidence bundle: token accounting CSV, consolidated latency JSON, Grafana snapshot URL, and a short run-notes markdown
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha Kapoor: Drafted initial spec and scope. Opted to prioritize determinism and reproducibility over adding chaotic co-tenant noise in v1.

2026-03-04 — Miguel Santos: Prototype harness (Go) created in github.com/redwood-inference/signature-runner PR#412. Initial run shows 12% variance due to clock drift between runners; working on sync layer.
2026-03-06 — Lena Cho (Design): Reviewed acceptance playbook UX. Requested a simpler 'one-click' customer run that wraps complex flags into a profile file (will add in next iteration).
2026-03-08 — Ravi Patel (SRE): Suggested we incorporate GPU power-capping tests to ensure throughput guarantees under thermal constraints; added to test matrix.
2026-03-10 — Miguel Santos: Replaced ad-hoc cron-based warmup with a tempo-controlled scheduler to reduce variance. Repeatability improved to ~4.2% across 5 runs in the staging cluster.
2026-03-12 — Security Review (note): Data handling covers anonymized traces only; retention policy set to 7 days for raw traces. Security sign-off pending for customer-shared artifacts.
notes: Design trade-offs: Using Go for the generator gives low-jitter scheduling and easy binary distribution for customers; k6 was evaluated but added variability due to JS runtime GC under high load.
Metric normalization: token costs are normalized to the customer-specified model context length; report will include cost-per-1k-tokens for standardization.
Autoscaler coupling: Tests will run with both conservative and aggressive policy presets; acceptance thresholds differ by preset and must be documented in the playbook.
Rollout plan: v1 harness in staging for internal validation (2 weeks), then pilot with two internal customers for onboarding. Iterate based on pilot feedback before GA.
